title: Make manual CI history complete and bounded audit failures diagnosable

source.ref: Combined manual run40239406031 exposed shallow HEAD and lifecycle probe failure; controlled load reproduces VM deadline failures

detail: The existing manual CI fetched main history but left its checked-out audit branch shallow. check:shipped-ids correctly refused the one-commit window. Fetch the actual GITHUB_SHA history as well, retaining the same seed date and guard floors. A real shallow file-remote fixture executes the actual workflow block: base-only fetch fails the guard floor, checkout-plus-base fetch passes. Combined Linux probes were inside unchanged CPU ceilings, but LIVE1317's probe failed with stderr discarded. Its exact remote reason was unavailable; controlled local contention reproduced14VM deadline failures in16runs. Precompile the same reviewed TypeScript source set before entering VM execution, so nested dependency compilation no longer consumes a parent's execution deadline. All16same-load runs then pass; all36email consequences and authored renderer checks remain. Keep1000ms VM deadlines, import allowlist, inert transports,120s command timeout and4500ms per-probe/linear total budgets unchanged. New tests still time out an infinite module body and reject an unreviewed import. Capture only first8KiB stderr per child, publish at most16lines for regressed done rows, preserve fd3CPU attribution, and keep expected open failures/stdout quiet. Fixture tests verify the bounds and verdicts. This repairs audit/CI evidence, not application email delivery or production behavior. A fresh exact-head combined run remains mandatory before claiming green.

verify.note: Actual bounded subprocess collector and CPU report plus workflow/deadline wiring. Real shallow-history, VM/hang/import and verdict/diagnostic behavior are normal test fixtures; no nested test suite in the backlog probe.
